claims.text: Moderate sliding wear in 3.5% NaCl dynamically transforms the surface of equimolar CoCrFeMnNi.
Sliding-induced shear produces an ultra-nanocrystalline or near-amorphous surface layer in equimolar CoCrFeMnNi.
The refined near-surface layer reinforces CoCrFeMnNi against mechanical material removal.
The ultra-nanocrystalline or amorphous layer stabilizes and maintains a protective passive oxide during sliding in a corrosive solution.
The dynamically formed layer provides synergistic resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion.
The initial equimolar CoCrFeMnNi alloy is coarse-grained and single-phase.
Severe shear deformation drives rapid grain refinement or tribo-induced amorphization at the CoCrFeMnNi surface.
A worn sample bearing the adaptive layer will have lower corrosion current density than the baseline.
A worn sample bearing the adaptive layer will have a more stable corrosion potential than the baseline.
Formation of the adaptive layer will reduce wear volume relative to samples experiencing sub-optimal sliding conditions.
Loads above an optimal threshold prevent effective formation or retention of the dynamic layer.
Excessively high loads cause both wear and corrosion performance to deteriorate.
Very low strain rates prevent the proposed dynamic surface restructuring.
The beneficial effect is confined to moderate combinations of sliding load and speed that permit adaptive-layer formation.

contradictions.description: The prediction includes reduced wear volume relative to an unworn baseline, but an unworn sample undergoes no sliding and therefore cannot provide a meaningful positive wear-volume comparator. A separately defined sub-optimal sliding control would be required.
